component.name: spring-redis
component.title: Spring Redis
component.description: Send commands to Redis and receive the messages of Redis Pub/Sub channels, using Spring Data Redis.
component.label: cache

redisTemplate.description: The org.springframework.data.redis.core.RedisTemplate that the producers of the endpoints of this component run the commands with, unless an endpoint sets its own redisTemplate. Autowired from the registry when it has exactly one RedisTemplate.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

CamelRedis.Command.label: producer
CamelRedis.Command.description: The name of the Redis command that the producer runs, such as GET or HSET, in any case. Replaces the command option for this message.

CamelRedis.Key.description: The key that the command works on, used by most commands, such as GET, SET, HSET, LPUSH, SADD and ZADD. For SDIFF, SINTER, SUNION, their STORE forms, ZINTERSTORE and ZUNIONSTORE, the first key, which is combined with the keys of the CamelRedis.Keys header.

CamelRedis.Keys.description: The keys to delete for DEL and to watch for WATCH, and for SDIFF, SINTER, SUNION, their STORE forms, ZINTERSTORE and ZUNIONSTORE the keys that are combined with the key of the CamelRedis.Key header. A collection of keys, or a String with one key or several keys separated by comma.

CamelRedis.Field.description: The field of the hash for HDEL, HEXISTS, HGET, HINCRBY, HSET and HSETNX.

CamelRedis.Fields.description: The fields of the hash to read for HMGET, and the keys to read for MGET.

CamelRedis.Value.description: The value for the commands that store, add or look up one value or member, such as SET, SETNX, GETSET, HSET, LPUSH, SADD, SISMEMBER, ZADD and GEOADD. It is a Long for INCRBY, DECRBY and HINCRBY, a Boolean for SETBIT, the new name of the key for RENAME and RENAMENX, and text for APPEND and ECHO. The serializer of the RedisTemplate writes it, so with the default JDK serializer it must be Serializable.

CamelRedis.Values.description: A Map of keys to values for MSET and MSETNX, and of fields to values for HMSET. For GEODIST, a Collection whose first two elements are the members to measure the distance between.

CamelRedis.Start.description: The index of the first element for LRANGE, LTRIM, ZRANGE, ZREVRANGE and ZREMRANGEBYRANK, the offset of the first byte for GETRANGE, and the minimum score for ZREMRANGEBYSCORE. Indexes start at 0, and a negative index counts from the end.

CamelRedis.End.description: The index of the last element, inclusive, for LRANGE, LTRIM, ZRANGE, ZREVRANGE and ZREMRANGEBYRANK, the offset of the last byte for GETRANGE, and the maximum score for ZREMRANGEBYSCORE. Indexes start at 0, and a negative index counts from the end, so -1 is the last element.

CamelRedis.Timeout.description: The time to live of the key in seconds for EXPIRE and SETEX, and in milliseconds for PEXPIRE. For BLPOP, BRPOP and BRPOPLPUSH, how many seconds to wait for an element while the list is empty.

CamelRedis.Offset.description: The offset of the bit for GETBIT and SETBIT, and the offset in bytes where SETRANGE writes the value.

CamelRedis.Destination.description: The key that receives the result for RPOPLPUSH, BRPOPLPUSH, SMOVE, SDIFFSTORE, SINTERSTORE, SUNIONSTORE, ZINTERSTORE and ZUNIONSTORE.

CamelRedis.Channel.description: The channel that PUBLISH posts the message to. The consumer sets it to the name of the channel that the message was received on.

CamelRedis.Message.description: The message that PUBLISH posts to the channel of the CamelRedis.Channel header. The serializer of the RedisTemplate writes it, so with the default JDK serializer it must be Serializable.

CamelRedis.Index.description: The index of the element of the list for LINDEX and LSET. Indexes start at 0, and a negative index counts from the end, so -1 is the last element.

CamelRedis.Position.description: Where LINSERT inserts the value: BEFORE or AFTER the pivot, in upper case.

CamelRedis.Pivot.description: The element of the list that LINSERT inserts the value before or after.

CamelRedis.Count.description: For LREM, how many elements equal to the value to remove: a positive count removes from the head, a negative count from the tail, and 0 removes all of them. For GEORADIUS and GEORADIUSBYMEMBER, the maximum number of members to return; if not set, all of them are returned.

CamelRedis.Timestamp.description: The time when the key expires, in seconds since the epoch for EXPIREAT and in milliseconds since the epoch for PEXPIREAT.

CamelRedis.Pattern.description: The glob-style pattern of the keys that KEYS returns, such as user:*. With the PSUBSCRIBE command, the consumer sets it, as a byte array, to the pattern of the channels option that the channel of the message matched.

CamelRedis.Db.description: The index of the database that MOVE moves the key to.

CamelRedis.Score.description: The score of the member that ZADD adds.

CamelRedis.Min.description: The minimum score, inclusive, for ZCOUNT, ZRANGEBYSCORE and ZREVRANGEBYSCORE.

CamelRedis.Max.description: The maximum score, inclusive, for ZCOUNT, ZRANGEBYSCORE and ZREVRANGEBYSCORE.

CamelRedis.Increment.description: The amount that ZINCRBY adds to the score of the member.

CamelRedis.WithScore.description: Whether ZRANGE and ZREVRANGE return the members together with their scores, as a Set of ZSetOperations.TypedTuple. If not set or false, they return the members only.

CamelRedis.Latitude.description: The latitude of the member that GEOADD adds, and of the center of the area that GEORADIUS searches.

CamelRedis.Longitude.description: The longitude of the member that GEOADD adds, and of the center of the area that GEORADIUS searches.

CamelRedis.Radius.description: The radius in meters of the area that GEORADIUS and GEORADIUSBYMEMBER search.

consumerOut.description: The message as the serializer reads it: with the default JDK serializer the Java object the publisher serialized, such as the String a PUBLISH of this component sent, with the channel in the CamelRedis.Channel header. A message the serializer cannot read, such as text from redis-cli, is given as its raw bytes: set a StringRedisSerializer as the serializer to receive text

producerIn.description: The body is not used: the key, the value and the other arguments of the command come from headers, such as CamelRedis.Key and CamelRedis.Value, or CamelRedis.Channel and CamelRedis.Message for PUBLISH. Set CamelRedis.Value from the body to store the body: with the default serializer it must be Serializable, so a stream fails

producerOut.description: The result of the command, which the CamelRedis.Command header can pick instead of the command option: SET, the default, PUBLISH and the other commands without a result keep the body; a Boolean or a number for those that test, count or increment, a Set or a List for those that read several members, a Map for HGETALL, and the stored object, which can be anything, for GET, HGET, LINDEX, LPOP, RPOP, SPOP and the other commands that read or pop one value: these are not known. These set the body to null when there is no value, such as GET of a missing key. An unknown command, or one the producer does not run, fails

host.description: The host name or IP address of the Redis server. The endpoint connects to it with the JedisConnectionFactory that it creates when connectionFactory is not set, and does not use it otherwise. If not set, localhost is used.

port.description: The port of the Redis server. The endpoint connects to it with the JedisConnectionFactory that it creates when connectionFactory is not set, and does not use it otherwise. If not set, 6379 is used.

channels.description: The channels that the consumer subscribes to, separated by comma. With the PSUBSCRIBE command they are patterns, such as news.*, and with SUBSCRIBE channel names. Required by the consumer. The producer does not use it: PUBLISH takes the channel from the CamelRedis.Channel header.

command.description: The Redis command that the producer runs, such as GET, SET or HSET. The CamelRedis.Command header replaces this option for a message. The consumer needs SUBSCRIBE or PSUBSCRIBE and fails to start with any other command, including the default SET. The producer fails a message with SUBSCRIBE, PSUBSCRIBE or a server command that it does not run, such as AUTH, FLUSHDB, INFO or SELECT.

connectionFactory.description: The org.springframework.data.redis.connection.RedisConnectionFactory that connects to Redis. The endpoint uses it for the RedisTemplate and the listener container that it creates, and then does not use host and port. If not set, the endpoint creates a JedisConnectionFactory for host and port, and destroys it when the endpoint shuts down.

redisTemplate.description: The org.springframework.data.redis.core.RedisTemplate that the producer runs the commands with, which also decides how keys and values are serialized. If not set, the redisTemplate of the component is used, and if that is not set either, the endpoint creates a RedisTemplate from connectionFactory and serializer. The consumer does not use it.

serializer.description: The org.springframework.data.redis.serializer.RedisSerializer for keys and values. The endpoint sets it as the default serializer of the RedisTemplate that it creates, and the consumer deserializes the body of each message with it. If not set, a JdkSerializationRedisSerializer is used, which stores keys and values in Java serialized form: use a StringRedisSerializer to work with text. The producer does not use it when a redisTemplate is set.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

listenerContainer.label: consumer,advanced
listenerContainer.description: The org.springframework.data.redis.listener.RedisMessageListenerContainer that the consumer subscribes to the channels with. If not set, the endpoint creates and starts one on connectionFactory, and destroys it when the endpoint shuts down.

deserializationFilter.label: advanced,security
deserializationFilter.description: An ObjectInputFilter pattern, in jdk.serialFilter syntax, that the default JdkSerializationRedisSerializer applies when it deserializes a value: the body of a message that the consumer receives, and a value that the producer reads with the RedisTemplate that the endpoint creates. If not set, the JVM-wide jdk.serialFilter is used when present, otherwise a default filter that rejects java.net.**, allows only java.**, javax.** and org.apache.camel.**, and limits the depth, references and size of the object graph. Not used when serializer is set.
